The largest possible value of n − a_n is 16, attained at n = 97.

**Reduction.** The integer 1 is always coprime to everything, so the condition says that no integer in 2..n is coprime to all of n, n+1, …, n+a. An integer k in 2..n is excluded exactly when some prime factor of k divides one of n, …, n+a. This holds for every such k if and only if every prime p ≤ n divides some number in that range. (The primes themselves are among the integers 2..n, so they are necessary, and they also suffice because every k ≥ 2 has a prime factor ≤ n.)

The next multiple of a prime p at or after n is n + ((−n) mod p). Hence

a_n = max over primes p ≤ n of ((−n) mod p).

**Bounding n − a_n.** Let q be the largest prime ≤ n. If q < n and q > n/2, then a_n ≥ 2q − n, so n − a_n ≤ 2n − 2q. If q = n, then q contributes 0 and the other primes decide a_n.

- n = 99: q = 97 gives a ≥ 95, so n − a ≤ 4.
- n = 98: q = 97 gives a ≥ 96, so n − a ≤ 2.
- n = 96: q = 89 gives a ≥ 82, so n − a ≤ 14.
- n = 95: q = 89 gives a ≥ 83, so n − a ≤ 12.
- n = 94: q = 89 gives a ≥ 84, so n − a ≤ 10.
- n = 93: q = 89 gives a ≥ 85, so n − a ≤ 8.
- n = 92 and n = 91: q = 89 gives a ≥ 86 and a ≥ 87, so n − a ≤ 6 and ≤ 4.
- n = 90: q = 89 gives a ≥ 88, so n − a ≤ 2.

**n = 97.** The distances to the next multiple, for the primes with the largest values, are:

| p | next multiple of p ≥ 97 | distance |
|---|---|---|
| 89 | 178 | 81 |
| 83 | 166 | 69 |
| 79 | 158 | 61 |
| 73 | 146 | 49 |
| 71 | 142 | 45 |
| 67 | 134 | 37 |
| 61 | 122 | 25 |
| 59 | 118 | 21 |

For p = 97 the distance is 0, and for the remaining primes below 59 it is smaller than 81. So a_97 = 81 and n − a_n = 16.

**Smaller n.** For n ≤ 89 the same bound is smaller:

- n = 89 has a_89 = 77 from p = 83, so n − a_n = 12.
- n = 88 has q = 83, so n − a_n ≤ 10.
- n = 83 has q = 79, so n − a_n ≤ 8.
- Smaller n give smaller values still.

ANSWER: 16
